system.biz: Northwind Supply's internal procurement platform. Employees request purchases, managers and finance approve them against cost-center budgets, buyers issue purchase orders, and accounts payable matches supplier invoices to those orders and pays vendors. NetSuite stays the system of record for the books.
system.tech: Six packages in a pnpm workspace: a Next.js portal acting as a BFF, the Fastify procure-api over Postgres, the invoicing worker fed by an SQS FIFO outbox, the nightly erp-sync job that talks to NetSuite over REST, shared zod contracts, and a legacy Express app that serves approve-by-link from emails.

caps.name: Purchase requests
caps.biz: Employees describe what they need, price it and send it for approval.

caps.name: Approvals
caps.biz: Rule-driven approval chains, delegation, SLA escalation and the notifications that ask people to decide.

caps.name: Budgets
caps.biz: Cost-center budgets: money is reserved on approval, released on cancel and consumed when invoices match.

caps.name: Purchase orders
caps.biz: Turning approved requests into purchase orders, amending them and recording goods received.

caps.name: Vendors and contracts
caps.biz: Onboarding suppliers, scoring their risk, holding bank and payout details, and getting contracts signed.

caps.name: Invoice matching
caps.biz: Getting supplier invoices in, reading them, and checking them against the PO and what was received before anyone pays.

caps.name: Vendor payments
caps.biz: The daily run that pays matched, budget-confirmed invoices to vendors, exactly once each.

caps.name: ERP sync
caps.biz: Keeping NetSuite and the platform in step every night: reference data in, POs and paid bills out.

caps.name: Platform and shared contracts
caps.biz: What every service leans on: auth, the database, the audit log, the event outbox, internal endpoints and the shared payload schemas.

ext:postgres.biz: Each service keeps its own data in its own Postgres database: procure-api the procurement records, invoicing the invoices and payments, erp-sync its sync ledger.
ext:postgres.tech: Plain pg pools with explicit transactions; BIGINT money columns are parsed as safe JS integers, and advisory locks keep scheduled jobs single-runner.

ext:sqs.biz: Carries procurement events (PO issued, amended, cancelled, goods received) from procure-api to invoicing so invoicing keeps working when procure-api is down.
ext:sqs.tech: One FIFO queue, procurement-events.fifo; MessageGroupId is the PO, MessageDeduplicationId the event id, and a redrive policy moves poison messages to a DLQ.

anchors.note: publish with group and dedup ids

ext:s3.biz: Stores the original PDF of every supplier invoice.
ext:s3.tech: Content-addressed keys (invoices/YYYY/MM/<sha256>.pdf) with KMS server-side encryption, written by the ingestion module.

ext:openai.biz: Reads invoice PDFs and pulls out vendor, PO number, lines and totals.
ext:openai.tech: Chat completions with the PDF attached and JSON mode at temperature 0; the reply is validated with a zod schema before it is stored.

ext:stripe.tech: Stripe Connect transfers to each vendor's connected account, with an idempotency key derived only from the invoice id.

ext:sendgrid.biz: Sends approval and status emails, and receives the emails suppliers send their invoices to.
ext:sendgrid.tech: @sendgrid/mail for outbound mail from procure-api; Inbound Parse posts emails to invoicing's /ingest/email, authenticated by a shared secret in the URL.

ext:slack.biz: Pings approvers and requesters by DM and posts overdue approvals to an escalations channel.
ext:slack.tech: @slack/web-api chat.postMessage with a Block Kit card linking to the portal.

ext:docusign.tech: docusign-esign with JWT user auth creates envelopes; DocuSign Connect calls back a public webhook verified by HMAC.

ext:netsuite.biz: The company ERP and the source of truth for cost centers, annual budgets and the chart of accounts; receives POs, vendor bills and payments.
ext:netsuite.tech: REST record API and SuiteQL over plain fetch with OAuth 1.0 token-based auth; writes carry X-NetSuite-Idempotency-Key and upsert by external id.

ext:sso.biz: The company single sign-on that logs users into the portal.
ext:sso.tech: The gateway mints a signed nw_session cookie (base64url JSON + HMAC-SHA256) that the portal verifies with SESSION_SECRET; unauthenticated users are redirected to SSO_LOGIN_URL.

portal/pages/requests.biz: Where employees see their purchase requests and create new ones.
portal/pages/requests.tech: Server components list requisitions from procure-api; the client form converts prices to cents, POSTs the draft to the BFF and optionally submits it in a second call.

portal/pages/approvals.biz: The approver's inbox of steps waiting for their decision.
portal/pages/approvals.tech: Server component reads /approvals/inbox; client buttons POST approve or reject (a comment is required to reject) to the BFF.

portal/pages/budgets.biz: Finance and approvers see each cost center's allocated, reserved, consumed and available money for the year.
portal/pages/budgets.tech: Server component over procure-api GET /budgets, restricted to finance and approver roles.

portal/pages/invoices.biz: Finance's queue of invoices that did not match, where they accept a variance or reject the invoice.
portal/pages/invoices.tech: Server component reads invoicing /invoices/awaiting-match; client actions POST a resolution with a mandatory note.

portal/pages/purchase-orders.biz: Detail view of one purchase order and its lines.
portal/pages/purchase-orders.tech: Server component fetching /purchase-orders/:id from procure-api, 404 when it does not exist.

portal/pages/vendors.biz: Searchable directory of vendors with their status and risk level.
portal/pages/vendors.tech: Server component over procure-api GET /vendors with an optional query.

portal/pages/shell.biz: The portal's frame: header and navigation, showing links by role.
portal/pages/shell.tech: Root layout that reads the session to decide which nav links to render.

portal/api/requisitions.biz: Browser entry point to create, submit and withdraw purchase requests.
portal/api/requisitions.tech: BFF route handlers that validate with the shared schemas and forward to procure-api with the service token and user header.

portal/api/approvals.biz: Browser entry point to record an approval decision.
portal/api/approvals.tech: BFF handler, approver role only, forwarding to procure-api POST /approvals/steps/:stepId/decision.

portal/api/invoices.biz: Browser entry point for finance to resolve an invoice exception.
portal/api/invoices.tech: BFF handler, finance role only, forwarding to invoicing POST /exceptions/:id/resolve.

portal/api/vendors.biz: Browser entry point to search vendors and onboard new ones.
portal/api/vendors.tech: BFF handlers over procure-api /vendors; onboarding is limited to buyers and finance.

portal/ui/components.biz: Shared form and display pieces: the line-item editor used on purchase requests and status badges.
portal/ui/components.tech: Client React components; line totals are computed in integer cents with the shared money helpers.

portal/lib/session.biz: Knows who is signed in and what they may do in the portal.
portal/lib/session.tech: Verifies the SSO gateway's signed nw_session cookie, gates pages and BFF calls by role, and builds the x-northwind-user header the backends trust; edge middleware only checks the cookie exists.

portal/lib/backend-clients.biz: The portal's way of talking to procure-api and invoicing without exposing backend tokens to the browser.
portal/lib/backend-clients.tech: fetch wrappers that attach the service token, caller name and user header; bff() wraps route handlers with session, role checks and error mapping.

procure-api/domain/requisitions.biz: Purchase requests: drafted with priced line items, edited while draft, submitted for approval or withdrawn.
procure-api/domain/requisitions.tech: Line numbering and totals in integer cents with spend grouped by category; submit moves draft to submitted through the audited transition and starts the approval chain in the same transaction.

procure-api/domain/approvals.biz: Decides who must approve a request, records their decisions, lets approvers delegate, and escalates steps that sit too long.
procure-api/domain/approvals.tech: Rules from the approval_rules table are matched (category rules on category spend) and built into steps with segregation of duties; the final approval reserves budget, emits requisition.approved and issues the PO when a vendor is set. A 15-minute job escalates overdue steps to the manager.

procure-api/domain/budgets.biz: Cost-center budgets per fiscal year: what is allocated, reserved by approved requests and consumed by matched invoices.
procure-api/domain/budgets.tech: Pure balance functions guard every reserve, release and consume against overspend; each movement is logged and audited. Cost centers and allocations are upserted from NetSuite, clamping allocations to what is already committed.

procure-api/domain/purchase-orders.biz: Purchase orders: issued from approved requests, amended or cancelled by buyers, received against, and closed once fully invoiced.
procure-api/domain/purchase-orders.tech: Every change checks the PO ceiling (never above the approved amount, never below what was invoiced or received), adjusts budget reservations, and writes an outbox event for invoicing.

procure-api/domain/vendors.biz: Supplier onboarding: KYB risk scoring, activation or rejection, suspension, bank accounts and the Stripe payout account.
procure-api/domain/vendors.tech: assessRisk blocks sanctions matches and embargoed countries and scores the rest; bank details are checksum-validated (IBAN mod-97, ABA) and stored masked.

procure-api/domain/contracts.biz: Vendor contracts sent out for e-signature and tracked until signed, declined or voided.
procure-api/domain/contracts.tech: The contract is saved as a draft, then sent through DocuSign outside the transaction; the Connect webhook verifies its HMAC and applies envelope status idempotently.

procure-api/domain/catalog.biz: Catalog search with the best vendor price, and importing carts from suppliers' punch-out sites.
procure-api/domain/catalog.tech: Price tiers pick the cheapest vendor unless a preferred vendor is within 5%; punch-out carts arrive as SAP OCI form posts and are mapped to line items via UNSPSC codes.

procure-api/platform/audit.biz: The append-only history of who changed what, which finance can read per entity.
procure-api/platform/audit.tech: transitionState is the only sanctioned status change: it locks the row, checks allowed source states, updates and inserts the audit event in the caller's transaction.

procure-api/platform/notifications.biz: Tells approvers they have something to decide, requesters what was decided, and finance when an approval is overdue.
procure-api/platform/notifications.tech: Best-effort email and Slack sends after commit, never failing the caller; approval emails carry HMAC-signed approve/reject links served by legacy-approvals.

procure-api/platform/queue.biz: Publishes procurement events for invoicing reliably: an event goes out if and only if the change that caused it committed.
procure-api/platform/queue.tech: Transactional outbox table relayed every 2 seconds to SQS FIFO with SKIP LOCKED; the relay stops at the first failure so later events for the same PO never overtake it.

procure-api/platform/internal.biz: Endpoints only the other services may call: invoicing reports matched invoices and reads payout accounts, erp-sync reads POs and pushes cost centers and GL accounts.
procure-api/platform/internal.tech: Fastify routes guarded by requireService for the named caller.

procure-api/platform/db.biz: procure-api's connection to its database and its schema migrations.
procure-api/platform/db.tech: pg pool with safe BIGINT parsing, DATE kept as strings, and a withTransaction helper; SQL migrations applied at startup.

procure-api/platform/http.biz: Starts procure-api, authenticates callers and turns errors into consistent responses.
procure-api/platform/http.tech: Fastify server with a shared bearer token plus x-northwind-caller allow-list, actor built from x-northwind-user, role guards, and an error handler mapping domain, zod and Postgres errors.

invoicing/ap/ingestion.biz: Takes supplier invoices in by email or portal upload and turns the PDF into structured data.
invoicing/ap/ingestion.tech: Stores the PDF in S3, dedupes by SHA-256 and by vendor invoice number, extracts fields with OpenAI, and parks inconsistent totals or low-confidence extractions as exceptions before matching.

invoicing/ap/matching.biz: Checks each invoice against its purchase order and what was actually received before it can be paid.
invoicing/ap/matching.tech: Pure three-way match with line pairing and basis-point price tolerances; on a match, reports the amount to procure-api to consume budget. New PO or receipt events re-run matching for parked invoices.

invoicing/ap/exceptions.biz: The queue of invoices that need a human, and how finance clears them.
invoicing/ap/exceptions.tech: One open exception per invoice; finance can accept a variance (then budget is confirmed) or reject the invoice, and system rematches supersede open exceptions.

invoicing/ap/invoices.biz: The invoice record and its status history, from received to paid.
invoicing/ap/invoices.tech: Repository with an atomic compare-and-set status transition that writes invoice_status_history, plus read queries for the portal and for erp-sync's paid-invoice feed.

invoicing/ap/payments.biz: Pays matched, budget-confirmed invoices to vendors once a day, and never pays the same invoice twice.
invoicing/ap/payments.tech: A scheduler behind a Postgres advisory lock starts the run; each invoice claims its single payments row and sends a Stripe transfer under an idempotency key derived only from the invoice id. Transient errors retry under the same key.

invoicing/ap/po-mirror.biz: invoicing's local copy of purchase orders and goods receipts, so matching never waits on procure-api.
invoicing/ap/po-mirror.tech: PO snapshots are applied only when their version is newer; receipts are inserted once and summed per line.

invoicing/platform/queue.biz: Receives the procurement events procure-api publishes.
invoicing/platform/queue.tech: SQS long-poll loop that validates each message with the shared schema, dispatches it, and deletes it only after handling; a failure stops the batch to keep FIFO order.

invoicing/platform/clients.biz: invoicing's calls back to procure-api when it needs an answer now.
invoicing/platform/clients.tech: fetch client for budget consumption and vendor payout accounts; 4xx answers are treated as decisions, not retried.

invoicing/platform/db.biz: invoicing's connection to its database and its schema migrations.
invoicing/platform/db.tech: pg pool, withTransaction helper and a startup migration runner.

invoicing/platform/http.biz: Starts the invoicing worker and its API, and decides who may call it.
invoicing/platform/http.tech: Fastify with multipart uploads; the inbound email route is public with its own secret, everything else needs the service token from portal or erp-sync. main.ts also starts the SQS consumer and payment scheduler.

erp-sync/sync/run.biz: The nightly job that brings NetSuite reference data in and pushes purchase orders and paid invoices out.
erp-sync/sync/run.tech: Runs under an advisory lock in a fixed order (cost centers, chart of accounts, POs, paid invoices); every write goes through syncOnce, and cursors never advance past an unsettled record.

erp-sync/sync/netsuite.biz: How erp-sync talks to NetSuite and translates platform records into NetSuite ones.
erp-sync/sync/netsuite.tech: Hand-written OAuth 1.0 TBA signing, a fetch client that classifies 429/5xx as retryable, paged SuiteQL, and mappers to purchase orders, vendor bills and payments keyed by nw-po/nw-bill/nw-pay external ids.

erp-sync/sync/sources.biz: erp-sync's reads from and writes to procure-api and invoicing.
erp-sync/sync/sources.tech: Cursor-paged async generators over the internal endpoints, plus PUTs of cost centers and GL accounts.

erp-sync/sync/ledger.biz: Remembers every write sent to NetSuite so nothing is sent twice and failures are retried, then handed to a human.
erp-sync/sync/ledger.tech: sync_ledger keyed by idempotency key with exponential backoff and a dead state after 8 attempts or a non-retryable error; forward-only cursors per source.

contracts/schemas/payloads.biz: The shared definition of every request and response that crosses a service boundary.
contracts/schemas/payloads.tech: zod schemas and inferred types for requisitions, approvals, POs, vendors, budgets, invoices and ERP sync, imported as TypeScript source through the workspace.

contracts/schemas/events.biz: The shape of the procurement events on the queue.
contracts/schemas/events.tech: A discriminated union of versioned event envelopes, and messageGroupId, which keys every PO event by its PO for FIFO ordering.

contracts/schemas/money.biz: Money handled the same way everywhere: whole cents, never floats.
contracts/schemas/money.tech: Currency and cents schemas, and helpers that multiply, sum and parse decimals while throwing instead of losing precision.

legacy-approvals/app/approve-by-link.biz: The page an approver lands on after clicking Approve or Reject in an email.
legacy-approvals/app/approve-by-link.tech: Express routes: GET only renders a confirmation because mail scanners prefetch links; POST verifies the token and forwards the decision to procure-api, mapping 409 and 403 to friendly pages.

legacy-approvals/app/link-token.biz: Checks that an email approval link is genuine and not expired.
legacy-approvals/app/link-token.tech: Verifies the base64url payload and HMAC-SHA256 signature with APPROVAL_LINK_SECRET; the format is shared byte for byte with procure-api's approval-link.ts.

legacy-approvals/app/procure-client.biz: Records the approver's decision in procure-api on their behalf.
legacy-approvals/app/procure-client.tech: axios client posting to /approvals/steps/:stepId/decision with the service token and a user header naming the approver.

flows.name: Submit a purchase request
flows.biz: From the request form to the first approver being notified.

steps.text: The form converts prices to cents, saves the draft and asks to submit it.
The BFF validates the body and forwards it to procure-api with the user header.
Creates the draft with numbered lines and a cents total, then moves it to submitted.
The status change and its audit event are written in one transaction.
Matches approval rules, builds the chain of approvers and inserts the steps.
After commit, emails and DMs the first approver.
Delivers the approval email with signed approve and reject links.
Sends a DM with a link to the portal.

flows.name: Approve a request into a purchase order
flows.biz: The last approval reserves budget, announces the approval and issues the PO.

steps.text: The approver clicks Approve in their inbox.
The BFF checks the approver role and forwards the decision.
Locks the step, checks the actor is the approver or a delegate, and records the decision.
With no step left, approves the requisition.
Reserves the total on the cost center, refusing to overspend.
Issues the PO if a vendor was chosen, within the approved amount.
Writes requisition.approved and purchase_order.issued to the outbox in the same transaction.

flows.name: Approve from an email link (legacy)
flows.biz: The older path: an approver decides from the email without opening the portal.

steps.text: Signs a token with step, approver, decision and expiry, and builds the link.
The link reaches the approver by email.
GET shows a confirmation page; POST acts on it.
Verifies the HMAC and expiry.
Posts the decision to procure-api on the approver's behalf.
The same decide path as the portal applies the decision.

flows.name: A PO reaches invoicing
flows.biz: How invoicing learns about POs and receipts without calling procure-api.

steps.text: Issuing, amending, cancelling or receiving goods enqueues an event.
The relay sends unsent outbox rows in order and stops at the first failure.
The FIFO queue keeps events for one PO in order and dedupes by event id.
The consumer validates the event and dispatches it.
Applies the PO snapshot only if its version is newer.
Re-runs matching for invoices parked waiting for this PO or receipt.

flows.name: Match a supplier invoice
flows.biz: From an emailed PDF to budget consumed on the PO.

steps.text: Inbound Parse posts the supplier's email with its PDF attachments.
Stores and dedupes the PDF, extracts fields, and parks bad extractions.
Keeps the original PDF under a content-addressed key.
Reads the PDF into JSON that is validated before use.
Three-way match of PO, receipts and invoice within tolerances.
Reports the matched amount to procure-api.
Internal endpoint accepts the call from invoicing only.
Records the invoiced amount and closes the PO when fully invoiced.
Consumes the budget, once per invoice.

flows.name: Daily payment run
flows.biz: Paying vendors for matched invoices, exactly once each.

steps.text: At the configured hour, one replica takes the advisory lock and starts the run.
Retries pending budget confirmations, then lists payable invoices due within the horizon.
Fetches each vendor's payout account fresh from procure-api.
Returns the Stripe account, payout currency and vendor status.
Claims the invoice's single payments row with its fixed idempotency key.
Creates the Connect transfer; a retry with the same key returns the original.

flows.name: Nightly NetSuite sync
flows.biz: Reference data in from NetSuite, POs and paid bills out to it.

steps.text: The CronJob takes the run lock and runs the steps in order.
Queries departments and budgets with SuiteQL.
NetSuite answers over its REST API.
Pushes cost centers to procure-api.
Upserts cost centers and allocations, clamping to committed spend.
Pushes changed POs, one write per PO version.
Skips writes that already succeeded and backs off failures.
Serves paid invoices since the cursor.
Creates a vendor bill from the PO, then the vendor payment.

decisions.name: SQS between procure-api and invoicing
decisions.note: invoicing used to call procure-api when an invoice arrived and stalled during month-end deploys; it now keeps a PO mirror fed by an outbox relayed to SQS FIFO.

decisions.name: Approval rules as data, not code
decisions.note: Thresholds change every budget cycle, so rules live in approval_rules and ship as SQL migrations finance reviews; git history is the policy history.

decisions.name: Money as integer cents end to end
decisions.note: Every amount is BIGINT cents from the portal form to the Stripe transfer; decimal strings exist only at the LLM-extraction and NetSuite boundaries.

decisions.name: Notifications are sent after commit and never fail the caller
decisions.note: A Slack or SendGrid outage must never roll back an approval decision.

decisions.name: Approve-by-link does not act on GET
decisions.note: Corporate mail scanners prefetch every link in an email; acting on GET once approved requests nobody had looked at.

concepts.name: Requisition
concepts.biz: A purchase request with priced lines, moving from draft to submitted, approved and ordered.

concepts.name: Purchase order
concepts.biz: The commitment to a vendor, versioned on every amendment.

concepts.name: Budget
concepts.biz: A cost center's money for one fiscal year: allocated, reserved, consumed.

concepts.name: Invoice
concepts.biz: A supplier's bill, from received through extracted, matched or exception, to paid.

concepts.name: Vendor
concepts.biz: A supplier with KYB risk, bank details and a Stripe payout account.

retiring.label: Being retired
retiring.note: Replaced by procure-api/approvals once approval emails link straight to the portal (PROC-412). Do not add features.
